serverMetadata.instructions:
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions.
CRITICAL: Before starting to work on a coding task, call the `initial_instructions` tool to read the 'Serena Instructions Manual'.

tools.description:
Use this tool to get a high-level understanding of the code symbols in a file.
This should be the first tool to call when you want to understand a new file, unless you already know
what you are looking for. Returns a JSON object containing symbols grouped by kind in a compact format.
tools.name: serena-get_symbols_overview

depth.description:
Depth up to which descendants shall be retrieved.
Default (-1) results in a language specific choice: 1 for java and kotlin and 0 for other languages.
depth.title: Depth

max_answer_chars.description:
If the overview is longer than this number of characters,
no content will be returned. -1 means the default value from the config will be used.
Don't adjust unless there is really no other way to get the content required for the task.
max_answer_chars.title: Max Answer Chars

relative_path.description: The relative path to the file to get the overview of.
relative_path.title: Relative Path

tools.description:
Finds symbols and code entities (classes, methods, etc.) based on the given name path pattern.
The returned symbol information can be used for edits or further queries.
Specify `depth > 0` to also retrieve children/descendants (e.g., methods of a class).

A name path is a path in the symbol tree *within a source file*.
For example, the method `my_method` defined in class `MyClass` would have the name path `MyClass/my_method`.
If a symbol is overloaded (e.g., in Java), a 0-based index is appended (e.g. "MyClass/my_method[0]") to
uniquely identify it.

To search for a symbol, you provide a name path pattern that is used to match against name paths.
It can be
 * a simple name (e.g. "method"), which will match any symbol with that name
 * a relative path like "class/method", which will match any symbol with that name path suffix
 * an absolute name path "/class/method" (absolute name path), which requires an exact match of the full name path within the source file.
Append an index `[i]` to match a specific overload only, e.g. "MyClass/my_method[1]". Returns symbols (with locations) matching the name.
tools.name: serena-find_symbol

depth.title: Depth

exclude_kinds.description: (optional) list of LSP symbol kinds (integers) to exclude.
exclude_kinds.title: Exclude Kinds

include_body.description: If True, include the symbol's source code. Use judiciously.
include_body.title: Include Body

include_info.description:
Whether to include additional info (hover-like, typically including docstring and signature),
about the symbol (ignored if include_body is True). Info is never included for child symbols.
Note: Depending on the language, this can be slow (e.g., C/C++).
include_info.title: Include Info

include_kinds.description: (optional) limits results to the given LSP symbol kinds (integers).
include_kinds.title: Include Kinds

max_matches.description:
Maximum number of permitted matches. If exceeded, a shortened result is returned
which allows refining the search. -1 (default) means no limit. Set to 1 to search for a unique symbol.
max_matches.title: Max Matches

name_path_pattern.description: The name path matching pattern (see above).
name_path_pattern.title: Name Path Pattern

relative_path.description:
(optional) restrict search to this file or directory. If None, searches entire codebase.
If a directory is passed, the search will be restricted to the files in that directory.
If a file is passed, the search will be restricted to that file.
If you have some knowledge about the codebase, you should use this parameter, as it will significantly
speed up the search as well as reduce the number of results.
relative_path.title: Relative Path

substring_matching.description:
If True, use substring matching for the last segment of `name_path_pattern`
(i.e. the name of the symbol, e.g. "foo" in "Class/foo" or "my_method" in "my_method").
substring_matching.title: Substring Matching

tools.description: Lists available memories, optionally filtered by topic.
tools.name: serena-list_memories

tools.description: Use to read a memory that is likely to be relevant to the current task, inferring relevance e.g. from the name.
tools.name: serena-read_memory

tools.description:
Use this to insert code after a class/method/function definition.
Don't use to insert after assignments (constants, fields).
tools.name: serena-insert_after_symbol

body.description:
The body/content to be inserted. The inserted code shall begin with the next line after
the symbol.
body.title: Body

name_path.description: Name path of the symbol after which to insert content.
name_path.title: Name Path

relative_path.description: The relative path to the file containing the symbol.
relative_path.title: Relative Path

tools.description: Finds implementations of the symbol at the given `name_path`. Returns a list of JSON objects with the symbols implementing the requested symbol.
tools.name: serena-find_implementations

exclude_kinds.description: (optional) list of LSP symbol kinds (integers) to exclude.
exclude_kinds.title: Exclude Kinds

include_info.description:
Whether to include additional info (hover-like, typically including docstring and signature),
about the implementing symbols.
include_info.title: Include Info

include_kinds.description: (optional) limits results to the given LSP symbol kinds (integers).
include_kinds.title: Include Kinds

relative_path.description:
The relative path to the file containing the symbol for which to find implementations.
Note that here you can't pass a directory but must pass a file.
relative_path.title: Relative Path

tools.description:
Replaces the body of the given symbol.

IMPORTANT: Only replace symbol bodies if you have previously made a retrieval with include_body=True and thus know what
constitutes the body!.
tools.name: serena-replace_symbol_body

body.description:
The new symbol body. The symbol body is the definition of a symbol
in the programming language, including e.g. the signature line for functions.
Depending on the language, it may or may not include a preceding docstring or other preceding annotations.
body.title: Body

name_path.description: Name path of the symbol whose body to replace.
name_path.title: Name Path

relative_path.description: The relative path to the file containing the symbol.
relative_path.title: Relative Path

tools.description:
Gets diagnostics for a file. Diagnostics are grouped as `relative_path -> severity -> name_path -> diagnostics_results`.
If a diagnostic cannot be mapped to a symbol, it is grouped under the special name path `<file>`. Returns grouped diagnostics for the requested file.
tools.name: serena-get_diagnostics_for_file

end_line.description: The last 0-based line to include. Defaults to -1, which means until the end of the file.
end_line.title: End Line

min_severity.description:
Minimum LSP severity to include, where 1=Error, 2=Warning, 3=Information, 4=Hint.
Diagnostics with lower-or-equal numeric severity are returned.
min_severity.title: Min Severity

relative_path.description: The relative path to the file to inspect.
relative_path.title: Relative Path

start_line.description: The first 0-based line to include. Defaults to 0.
start_line.title: Start Line

tools.description:
Finds references to the symbol at the given `name_path`. The result will contain metadata about the referencing symbols
as well as a short code snippet around the reference. Returns a list of JSON objects with the symbols referencing the requested symbol.
tools.name: serena-find_referencing_symbols

exclude_kinds.description: Optional list of LSP symbol kinds (integers) to exclude.
exclude_kinds.title: Exclude Kinds

include_kinds.description: (optional) limits results to the given LSP symbol kinds (integers).
include_kinds.title: Include Kinds

relative_path.description: The relative path to the file containing the symbol for which to find references.
relative_path.title: Relative Path

tools.description:
Inserts the given content before the beginning of the definition of the given symbol (via the symbol's location).
A typical use case is to insert a new class, function, method, field or variable assignment; or
a new import statement before the first symbol in the file.
tools.name: serena-insert_before_symbol

body.description: The body/content to be inserted before the line in which the referenced symbol is defined.
body.title: Body

name_path.description: Name path of the symbol before which to insert content.
name_path.title: Name Path

relative_path.description: The relative path to the file containing the symbol.
relative_path.title: Relative Path

# adlc_contract — kestrel-services

Derived from AGENTS.md by `adlc baseline`; do not edit here, edit AGENTS.md.

## Build, test, run, lint
- Three independent services; build and test each in its own directory (see the service
  `AGENTS.md` files): `booking/` (Maven), `pricing/` (dotnet), `gateway/` (uv + pytest).
- The oracle for "an edit landed" is that service's test suite. Cross-service edits must
  keep all three green.
- Local run: each service starts on its own port; the gateway reads `BOOKING_BASE_URL` and
  `PRICING_BASE_URL`.

## Conventions
- Wire format is snake_case JSON everywhere (Jackson SNAKE_CASE, System.Text.Json
  SnakeCaseLower, Pydantic aliases). Internal code follows each language's idiom.
- Money is decimal, minor units, rounded AwayFromZero (ADR-0005 in kestrel-ops).
- Errors are RFC 7807 problem details with a stable `detail` string; those strings are
  contract (the gateway matches on them).
- Ticket ids (`BOOK-`, `PRC-`, `GW-`) appear in commit messages and comments; the ticket
  notes live in kestrel-ops, not here.

## Do not touch
- `booking/src/main/resources/db/` — schema and seed are owned by booking + platform; a
  change needs a migration ticket.
- Anything under `pricing/src/Kestrel.Pricing/Tariffs/Data/` — tariff data is loaded by
  configuration; classes there may look unreferenced and still be live.
- `gateway/gateway/legacy/` — scheduled for removal under its own ticket; do not extend.

## Where things are explained
- ADRs, runbooks, postmortems and ticket notes: the kestrel-ops repo (`kestrel-ops:adr/`,
  `kestrel-ops:runbooks/`, `kestrel-ops:postmortems/`, `kestrel-ops:tickets/`). Ownership: `CODEOWNERS`.

<!-- adlc:routing:start -->

## Service: booking
Service-level notes for `booking/` (root `AGENTS.md` still applies).

- Build/test here: `mvn -q test` (JUnit 5, H2 under the `test` profile).
- Entry point: `src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/BookingApplication.java`.
- Wire contract: `POST/GET /v2/shipments`, `POST /v2/shipments/{id}/reserve`, `GET /v2/carriers`;
  response shape is `ShipmentResponse` (snake_case, includes `eta_confidence`). The gateway
  and the web app depend on it.
- Properties live in `src/main/resources/application.yml`; feature flags are under
  `kestrel.booking.features.*`.
- Do not touch: `src/main/resources/db/`.

## Service: gateway
Service-level notes for `gateway/` (root `AGENTS.md` still applies).

- Build/test here: `uv venv -p 3.12 .venv && uv pip install -p .venv/bin/python -e ".[dev]"`,
  then `.venv/bin/pytest -q` (respx mocks; no live upstreams needed).
- Entry point: `gateway/main.py` (FastAPI app factory).
- Wire contract: public `/api/*` routes; upstream clients in `gateway/clients/` call
  booking `/v2/*` and pricing `/v1/*`. Response models in `gateway/models.py` are what
  the web app sees.
- Settings via environment (`gateway/settings.py`): `BOOKING_BASE_URL`, `PRICING_BASE_URL`,
  `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `KESTREL_FEATURE_MULTI_CARRIER_QUOTES`.
- Do not touch: `gateway/legacy/`.

## Service: pricing
Service-level notes for `pricing/` (root `AGENTS.md` still applies).

- Build/test here: `dotnet test` from this directory (xunit).
- Entry point: `src/Kestrel.Pricing/Program.cs`; solution `Kestrel.Pricing.sln`.
- Wire contract: `POST /v1/quote` → `quote_id, amount, currency, breakdown[]`;
  `GET /v1/carriers/{code}/surcharges`. The gateway depends on both.
- Configuration: `src/Kestrel.Pricing/appsettings.json` (`Pricing:*`, `TariffLoader`).
  Types named in configuration are loaded by name — grep for the type name in JSON
  before calling anything dead.
- Do not touch: `src/Kestrel.Pricing/Tariffs/Data/`.

## Context layer
- context: graphify, serena
- artifact: `graphify-out/graph.json` (check `adlc stale`)
- sensitive paths: none declared

# adlc_contract — kestrel-services

Derived from AGENTS.md by `adlc baseline`; do not edit here, edit AGENTS.md.

## Build, test, run, lint
- Three independent services; build and test each in its own directory (see the service
  `AGENTS.md` files): `booking/` (Maven), `pricing/` (dotnet), `gateway/` (uv + pytest).
- The oracle for "an edit landed" is that service's test suite. Cross-service edits must
  keep all three green.
- Local run: each service starts on its own port; the gateway reads `BOOKING_BASE_URL` and
  `PRICING_BASE_URL`.

## Conventions
- Wire format is snake_case JSON everywhere (Jackson SNAKE_CASE, System.Text.Json
  SnakeCaseLower, Pydantic aliases). Internal code follows each language's idiom.
- Money is decimal, minor units, rounded AwayFromZero (ADR-0005 in kestrel-ops).
- Errors are RFC 7807 problem details with a stable `detail` string; those strings are
  contract (the gateway matches on them).
- Ticket ids (`BOOK-`, `PRC-`, `GW-`) appear in commit messages and comments; the ticket
  notes live in kestrel-ops, not here.

## Do not touch
- `booking/src/main/resources/db/` — schema and seed are owned by booking + platform; a
  change needs a migration ticket.
- Anything under `pricing/src/Kestrel.Pricing/Tariffs/Data/` — tariff data is loaded by
  configuration; classes there may look unreferenced and still be live.
- `gateway/gateway/legacy/` — scheduled for removal under its own ticket; do not extend.

## Where things are explained
- ADRs, runbooks, postmortems and ticket notes: the kestrel-ops repo (`kestrel-ops:adr/`,
  `kestrel-ops:runbooks/`, `kestrel-ops:postmortems/`, `kestrel-ops:tickets/`). Ownership: `CODEOWNERS`.

<!-- adlc:routing:start -->

## Service: booking
Service-level notes for `booking/` (root `AGENTS.md` still applies).

- Build/test here: `mvn -q test` (JUnit 5, H2 under the `test` profile).
- Entry point: `src/main/java/com/kestrel/booking/BookingApplication.java`.
- Wire contract: `POST/GET /v2/shipments`, `POST /v2/shipments/{id}/reserve`, `GET /v2/carriers`;
  response shape is `ShipmentResponse` (snake_case, includes `eta_confidence`). The gateway
  and the web app depend on it.
- Properties live in `src/main/resources/application.yml`; feature flags are under
  `kestrel.booking.features.*`.
- Do not touch: `src/main/resources/db/`.

## Service: gateway
Service-level notes for `gateway/` (root `AGENTS.md` still applies).

- Build/test here: `uv venv -p 3.12 .venv && uv pip install -p .venv/bin/python -e ".[dev]"`,
  then `.venv/bin/pytest -q` (respx mocks; no live upstreams needed).
- Entry point: `gateway/main.py` (FastAPI app factory).
- Wire contract: public `/api/*` routes; upstream clients in `gateway/clients/` call
  booking `/v2/*` and pricing `/v1/*`. Response models in `gateway/models.py` are what
  the web app sees.
- Settings via environment (`gateway/settings.py`): `BOOKING_BASE_URL`, `PRICING_BASE_URL`,
  `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `KESTREL_FEATURE_MULTI_CARRIER_QUOTES`.
- Do not touch: `gateway/legacy/`.

## Service: pricing
Service-level notes for `pricing/` (root `AGENTS.md` still applies).

- Build/test here: `dotnet test` from this directory (xunit).
- Entry point: `src/Kestrel.Pricing/Program.cs`; solution `Kestrel.Pricing.sln`.
- Wire contract: `POST /v1/quote` → `quote_id, amount, currency, breakdown[]`;
  `GET /v1/carriers/{code}/surcharges`. The gateway depends on both.
- Configuration: `src/Kestrel.Pricing/appsettings.json` (`Pricing:*`, `TariffLoader`).
  Types named in configuration are loaded by name — grep for the type name in JSON
  before calling anything dead.
- Do not touch: `src/Kestrel.Pricing/Tariffs/Data/`.

## Context layer
- context: graphify, serena
- artifact: `graphify-out/graph.json` (check `adlc stale`)
- sensitive paths: none declared
